title: ResourceSaver serialization issue for inner classes
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in Godot v4.5.1.stable 

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Single-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 7 265K (20 threads) - 31.37 GiB memory

### Issue description

When a Resource contains an `@export` property referencing an inner/nested class instance, the resource fails to deserialize properly after saving. The inner class serializes as an anonymous GDScript sub-resource, but when loaded, the property becomes `null`.

**Expected behavior:**
The `roster_position` property should deserialize correctly, maintaining its reference to the inner class instance with all properties intact.

**Actual behavior:**
After loading, the `roster_position` property is `null`, causing runtime errors when accessed:
```
Invalid access to property or key 'short_name' on a base object of type 'Nil'.
```

**Root cause:**
The saved `.tres` file contains anonymous GDScript sub-resources that cannot be reconstructed during deserialization:
```tres
[sub_resource type="GDScript" id="GDScript_6ah8u"]

[sub_resource type="Resource" id="Resource_ns4hl"]
script = SubResource("GDScript_6ah8u")
short_name = "A2"
long_name = "Attack 2"
```

Godot cannot resolve the anonymous GDScript reference back to the inner class definition.

**Workaround:**
Move each inner class to a separate `.gd` file with its own `class_name` declaration. With named classes in separate files, serialization correctly references the class by name and deserialization works as expected.

**Impact:**
This prevents using inner classes for type-safe enums or lightweight class hierarchies within serialized Resources, forcing developers to create many small files for what could logically be grouped as inner classes.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a script with inner classes (NOTE: I've tested this with extending both Node and Resource in class, the behavior is the same):
```gdscript
class_name RosterPositions
extends Node

class RosterPosition:
    extends Resource
    @export var short_name: String

class Attack2:
    extends RosterPosition
    func _init() -> void:
        short_name = "A2"
```

Create a resource that references the inner class:
```gdscript
class_name PlayPositionData
extends Resource

@export var roster_position: RosterPositions.RosterPosition
```

Save and load the resource:
```gdscript
var data = PlayPositionData.new()
data.roster_position = RosterPositions.Attack2.new()
ResourceSaver.save(data, "user://test.tres")

var loaded = load("user://test.tres") as PlayPositionData
print(loaded.roster_position)
```

The inner class instance is lost during deserialization.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[inner_class_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23657153/inner_class_mrp.zip)
